items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

Black History Month has been recognized in Canada since 1978 when advocates from the Ontario Black History Society emphasized the importance of this celebration for Canadians of all races. Almost fifty years of celebration of Black history and Black excellence are still underlined by the struggles that come with the Black experience.

Black communities are still underrepresented in workplaces and decision-making structures, more negatively affected in health outcomes, lacking appropriate ongoing investments for entrepreneurs and more. In communities across Canada and locally, we have also seen that racialized individuals face extreme backlash when they speak out against injustices.

We all have a role in creating a city that brings an end to racial discrimination, and to build a more inclusive community. This starts with the basics of how we relate to each other as humans -- we must be aware of our individual prejudice and learn to treat each other with dignity, respect and compassion. Learning about the experiences of others is an essential part of understanding how we can effectively join in the fight against all forms of racism and discrimination, including anti-Black racism.

Throughout February, we encourage you to support local Black-owned businesses, read the work of Black writers and connect with your community at one of the many events being hosted by local organizations.

As a Council, we reaffirm our commitment to addressing anti-Black racism and rededicate ourselves to making the City of Waterloo a place where the contributions of Black community members are recognized and celebrated.
Councillor Roach offered further remarks on the importance of diversity.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment No. 49
notes: & Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-13
446 Albert Inc, 446 Albert Street
Prepared by: Amanda Wyszynski
Ward No.: Ward 6 – Central Columbia
Amanda Wyszynski gave a presentation with an overview of the proposed development and the requested Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments. She then responded to questions of Council.
Brandon Simon, Associate, The Planning Partnership gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development. He then responded to questions of Council.
Andrew Steinsky, Paradigm Transportation also responded to questions of Council.
Amanda Wyszynski and Joel Cotter also responded to questions of Council.

Judith Fletcher, Resident of Waterloo gave a presentation objecting to the rezoning to high density, speaking instead in favour of rezoning to medium density and in protecting the surrounding greenspace. She then responded to questions of Council.

Elisabeth Parsons, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the environmental impact of big developments, and where they fit into the big picture of the City’s plan. She also spoke about the traffic issues in the area. Amanda Wyszynski, Joel Cotter and Bob Henderson responded to questions of Council. Brandon Simon, Associate, The Planning Partnership also responded to questions of Council.
Dev Handa, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the proposed amendments, and against the plan to move to high density. He also spoke about the traffic issues in the area.
Ashwin Annamalai, Resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of more housing, especially for the student population.
Shiva Subramanian, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the bigger picture of the housing crisis, and the need for more two and three bedroom apartments.
Craig Sloss, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the impacts on the future budget for a development that is already on a site that’s already serviced.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: New Business
notes: Mayor McCabe made a statement regarding the Housing Accelerator Fund amount of $22 million that the City is receiving from the Federal Government. She wanted to thank all the staff that worked together to make this happen.

Councillor Vasic was at a Rotary Club meeting on January 30 where they awarded the two folks who organize Wonders of Winter with the Paul Harris Fellowship Award. They also gave their appreciation to Parks staff for their assistance with Wonders of Winter.

Councillor Wright mentioned that a new piece of art was unveiled in Uptown North at Brighton Park, with the help of the Neighbourhoods team. It is a woven wall by artist Agnes Niewiadomski, with the launch on Saturday, February 3.

Councillor Roe helped out at the Feeding Frenzi at the Waterloo Pentecostal Assembly on Thursday, February 1, which is a community support initiative for college and university students. She gave a shout out to the organizers and volunteers for their work supporting students.

Councillor Freeman spent an hour at Lester B Pearson Public School with grade five students, talking about local government on Friday, February 2. She reminded everyone that Mayor and Council for a Day is coming up.

Councillor Freeman added that the Housing Accelerator Fund announcement at Parkwood was meaningful, and it’s important to recognize how much the suburbs are becoming urban areas and that the City is changing.
Mayor McCabe also mentioned the pre-budget submission that has been made to the Province. The full release can be found on the City’s website.
